title: Lachy Groom backs Indian startup aiming to keep aircraft aloft for a year
slides: Lachy Groom bets on an Indian startup. Why?
They aim to keep aircraft flying for a year.
The secret isn't new engines—it's smarter maintenance.
Your airline's downtime could shrink dramatically.
Watch this space—or your next flight may change.
thread_text:
1. Why a $100M bet?

Lachy Groom just backed an Indian startup that promises to keep planes flying for a year straight.

2. No new engines here

The secret isn't hardware—it's predictive maintenance using AI to spot failures before they happen.

3. Downtime shrinks, profits soar

Airlines could cut unscheduled groundings dramatically, saving millions and boosting fleet utilization.

4. Your flight gets cheaper? Maybe

Lower maintenance costs could mean lower ticket prices—or fatter margins for carriers.

5. Watch your next booking

Check if your airline uses predictive maintenance. If not, ask why—your departure time might depend on it.

instagram.caption:
Your next flight might not be delayed because of a mechanical issue. A startup backed by investor Lachy Groom is using AI to predict part failures before they happen, keeping planes in the air for up to a year without unscheduled groundings. No new engines, just smarter maintenance. ✈️

Airlines could save millions by cutting downtime, and that might mean cheaper tickets or better routes for you. But only if carriers actually adopt this tech. 🔧

For anyone covering aviation, tech, or business: your next story could be about which airline is quietly testing this—and which one isn't. Check your own flight's on-time record. Is your carrier still flying blind? 🤔
